paperTitle: Evaluation of Pose Estimation for Fall Detection Systems
centralContribution: This work evaluates the effectiveness of pose estimation methods as a feature extraction solution for fall detection systems, demonstrating that combining state-of-the-art pose estimation frameworks with a simple neural network classifier achieves competitive results against sensor and other camera-based solutions on the UR Fall Detection dataset.

units.title: Paper Abstract
units.summary: Addresses fall detection using pose estimation from standard video.

content.description: Falls among the elderly are a leading cause of injury, necessitating effective fall detection. Existing solutions like wearables or ambient sensors have limitations. Traditional camera-based methods are often complex or require specialized hardware. This paper proposes using pose estimation, a hardware-agnostic method, to extract semantic-rich human joint location information from standard RGB video as features for fall detection.

units.title: System Pipeline Overview
units.summary: Visual overview of the fall detection system pipeline.

content.caption: Proposed Fall Detection System Pipeline
content.description: A conceptual illustration of the proposed system pipeline, where raw RGB video frames are processed by one of three state-of-the-art pose estimation frameworks (OpenPose, AlphaPose, PoseNet) to extract 3 * K pose feature vectors. These vectors are then fed into a simple fully-connected neural network classifier, which outputs a fall probability via a sigmoid activation function.
